results.content: # Stopping Rules and Dose Limiting Toxicity (DLT) Criteria in Phase 1 Trials. Stopping Rules and Dose Limiting Toxicity (DLT) Criteria in Phase 1 Trials. # Stopping Rules and Dose Limiting Toxicity (DLT). One of the most critical aspects of early-phase trial design is the implementation of **stopping rules and Dose Limiting Toxicity (DLT) criteria**. These safety mechanisms ensure that trials are halted or adjusted when adverse events (AEs) suggest that further exposure at a given dose is unethical or potentially harmful. ## What Are Dose Limiting Toxicities (DLTs)? They help determine the *maximum tolerated dose (MTD)* and inform decisions about escalation, de-escalation, or stopping. Any event that qualifies as a DLT within this window may affect cohort progression or trial continuation. ## What Are Stopping Rules? **Stopping rules** are prespecified safety conditions that, if triggered, lead to the temporary or permanent halt of:. * Dose escalation to the next cohort. ## Types of Stopping Rules. * If ≥2 out of 6 participants at a dose level experience DLTs, escalation is halted. Pharmacokinetic (PK)-Driven Stopping Rules. ## Designing DLT and Stopping Rules in Protocols. Stopping rules and DLT definitions must be clearly described in the protocol. In many early-phase trials, a Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) or **Safety Review Committee (SRC)** is established. * Reviews all AE and DLT data after each cohort. ## Real-World Example: How DLT Criteria Stopped a Trial. As per the stopping rule of ≥2 DLTs in 6 subjects, escalation was paused. ## Adaptive Escalation with Stopping Rules. Modern dose escalation designs (like CRM or BOIN) incorporate stopping rules algorithmically:. * **FDA**: Expects stopping rules to be pre-specified in the protocol under IND. * **EMA**: Requires stopping rules and DLT definitions per “Guideline on strategies to identify and mitigate risks for FIH and early clinical trials.”. * Define both drug-related and unrelated stopping rules (e.g., device failure, protocol deviation). * Conduct simulations to validate stopping rule robustness before trial start. Stopping rules and DLT criteria serve as critical safeguards in Phase 1 clinical trials.

results.title: Understanding Thermal Ramp Rates in Environmental Testing - Environmental Test Chambers
results.content: ## Understanding Thermal Ramp Rates in Environmental Testing. **Thermal ramp rate** refers to how quickly the temperature inside a test chamber increases or decreases over time. This rate plays a critical role in **product qualification, stress screening, and accelerated life testing**, especially in industries like electronics, aerospace, automotive, and battery development. In this article, we break down what ramp rates are, why they matter, and how to select the right chamber for your application. ## **What Is a Thermal Ramp Rate?**. **Ramp rate** is the **rate of temperature change** inside an environmental test chamber, usually measured in **°C per minute** (e.g., 5°C/min). * A **negative ramp** means cooling the chamber. For example, a chamber with a 10°C/min ramp rate can go from 20°C to 70°C in just 5 minutes. ## **Why Ramp Rates Matter in Environmental Testing**. Many industry standards like **MIL-STD-810**, **JEDEC JESD22-A104**, and **IEC 60068** require specific ramp rates for thermal cycling or shock testing. Faster ramp rates mean shorter test cycles, improving throughput and lab productivity. ### **Soak with Ramp**. ## **Typical Ramp Rate Ranges by Application**. ## **How to Choose a Chamber Based on Ramp Rate Needs**. * **Chamber volume** — larger chambers often have slower ramp rates. Chambers from **T3 EnviroCorp** are optimized for ramp-rate stability even under load, with high-performance airflow, precision PID control, and real-time logging. ## **Test Standards That Specify Ramp Rates**. * **JEDEC JESD22-A104D**: Thermal cycling for semiconductor devices with max ramp rates. * **IEC 62133 / UN 38.3**: Battery testing protocols that define controlled ramp rates for safety. ## **Best Practices for Ramp Rate Testing**. Ensure ramp rates are being accurately achieved and logged. Reduce thermal shock on sensitive units with gradual pre-ramp steps. Thermal ramp rates are more than a technical spec — they directly impact **test validity**, **product durability**, and **certification readiness**. Whether you’re screening for solder cracks, validating a BMS system, or qualifying a satellite component, ramp rate matters. results.title: Swiss animal welfare labelling rules: A ‘learning curve’ for producers
results.content: # Swiss animal welfare labelling rules: A ‘learning curve’ for producers. Europe’s producers are well placed to adapt to Switzerland’s new animal welfare labelling rules, and harmonised EU regulation could be around the corner, says poultry industry association AVEC. At the start of July, new animal welfare labelling requirements came into effect in Switzerland for food products of animal origin. Under the new rules, meat, dairy and eggs from animals subjected to any painful procedures without anaesthesia or stunning must be clearly labelled as such. In terms of what this means for their producers, Birthe Steenberg, AVEC's secretary general, the association of poultry processors and poultry trade in the EU, told Fi Global Insights: “In practical terms, any country-specific labelling scheme introduces a learning curve for producers who trade with that country.”. “We are confident that countries and companies exporting to Switzerland will continue to supply the country with high quality products in alignment with the new framework either by adopting the required labelling or adapting their production criteria, managing the transition at individual country or company level.”. Asked what AVEC thought of the new rules, Steenberg said that in principle, the association welcomed initiatives on transparent labelling. The Swiss decision to regulate on animal welfare labelling has come at a time when the Commission has been stalling on this topic. “Currently there are no harmonised animal welfare labelling rules in the EU. In the absence of EU-wide legislation, several member states operate their own public and/or private, mainly voluntary, animal welfare labelling schemes, each built on different criteria,” Steenberg explained. It looked as though the harmonisation might be imminent in 2019, when the EU Council asked the Commission to assess the need for and impact of an EU regulatory framework with criteria for animal welfare labelling schemes. To this end, the Commission established a subgroup on animal welfare labelling under the EU Platform on Animal Welfare. “As of recently, the Commission has entered a new consultation phase aimed at modernising the existing animal welfare framework, including a potential proposal on labelling,” she added. A freelance journalist for over 20 years, Lynda has extensive experience in covering food industry developments for the B2B media.

results.content: # Pre-Clinical Testing in Drug Development: Role of Animal Studies in Safety, Toxicity, and Pharmacological Assessment # **Pre-Clinical Testing in Drug Development: Role of Animal Studies in Safety, Toxicity, and Pharmacological Assessment** ***STEP FOR NEW DRUG APPROVAL IN INDIA*** *1.Drug Discovery: New compound or molecule is identified.* Pre-Clinical Testing: Conducted on animals to assess safety, toxicity, and pharmacology.* Apply to CDSCO: Submit Form CT-04 to get approval for human clinical trials.* Clinical Trials (as per NDCT Rules, 2019):* *Phase I: Safety on healthy volunteers.* *Phase II: Efficacy and side effects on patients.* *Phase III: Large-scale testing on diverse populations.* New Drug Application (NDA): Submit Form CT-21 to CDSCO for marketing approval.* Review by SEC: Expert committee evaluates safety, efficacy, and quality.* DCGI Approval: Drugs Controller General of India gives final nod.* Manufacturing License: Obtained from State Licensing Authority.* Marketing & Phase IV: Post-marketing surveillance to monitor long-term safety.* *This process ensures that every new drug in India is tested thoroughly for safety and effectiveness before public use.* # *Pre-Clinical Testing in Drug Development: Role of Animal Studies in Safety, Toxicity, and Pharmacological Assessment* Drug development is a rigorous, multi-stage process designed to ensure that new pharmaceutical compounds are **safe, effective, and of high quality** before they are introduced into the human population. In India, like in many other countries, pre-clinical testing is governed by a **robust regulatory framework** that ensures both **scientific reliability and ethical standards**. ## **Regulatory Framework in India** The **NDCT Rules, 2019**, lay down the requirements for conducting pre-clinical studies, including: The **Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940** also governs pre-clinical testing through various rules ensuring ethical and scientific standards. results.title: National Beef Welfare Scheme Deadline | agridirect.ie
results.content: The Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine has confirmed that applications for the National Beef Welfare Scheme will close on the 12th of September. As of the 5th of September, DAFM had received almost 7,400 applications from farmers across the country. Eligible farmers who have not yet applied for the National Beef Welfare Scheme are urged to do so immediately. Payment for IBR sampling will range from €120 to €300 depending on the number of animals tested. In order to receive this payment, you will have to engage a veterinarian to select, blood sample and test up to 20 animals for Infectious Bovine Rhinotracheitis antibodies. The inclusion of IBR testing as a requirement for this scheme has been the subject of significant criticism from farming organisations, with some representative bodies regarding it as evidence of the Government's unwillingness to consult with farmers on issues of animal health.
